title: Plan to End Chronic Homelessness endorsed in principle
subtitle: Committee also backed Indigenous-led child care at two Region-leased sites; delegations urged funding and area municipality involvement.
overview: The Community and Health Services Committee spent most of the day on the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness. More than a dozen delegates, including community partners and people with lived experience, spoke, nearly all in support. One organization asked the committee not to endorse the plan as drafted. The plan sets a goal of functional zero chronic homelessness by 2030 and contains 30 actions.

The committee recommended that Council accept the plan in principle {{vote:m3}}. An amendment {{vote:m2}} directs staff to add area municipalities to the co-creators group and to develop a detailed plan of recommendations, including funding and advocacy actions, for the 2025 Regional Budget process. Residents should expect the costs and the advocacy asks to be set out then.

The committee also recommended that staff explore leasing two Region-owned sites, in Cambridge and Kitchener, to non-profit organizations for culturally responsive child care for Indigenous children and families {{vote:m4}}. The committee also received a paramedic community program report on the consent agenda {{vote:m1}}. After the meeting, the committee went into closed session on land acquisition and a personnel matter.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council accept the plan in principle as the official plan to prevent, address and end homelessness in Waterloo Region, with the amendment's added direction {{vote:m3}}.

decisions.item: Amendment on area municipalities and funding
decisions.detail: The committee recommended directing staff to add area municipalities to the co-creators group and to bring a detailed plan with funding and advocacy actions to the 2025 budget process {{vote:m2}}.

The committee recommended that staff explore opportunities and identify non-profit organizations to lease 30 Christopher Drive, Cambridge and 104 Stirling Avenue South, Kitchener for child care serving Indigenous children and families and others facing systemic barriers.
The committee received for information the Paramedic Services 2023 Community Paramedicine Program report, the only consent item.

debate: Delegates who supported the plan called it community-built, evidence-based and prevention-focused. Several said it needs adequate funding, advocacy to the provincial and federal governments, and involvement of area municipalities.

One delegate opposed endorsement, arguing the plan does not address root causes such as trauma, mental health and community reintegration, and lacks a seniors focus. The delegate asked for a delay to add these. A few councillors shared concerns about missing root causes.

Some councillors said Council had little chance to take part in developing the plan. They called it philosophical rather than specific, and said terms such as human rights and functional zero were not clearly defined. Staff replied that Council directed the work in August 2022 and received several updates, that the plan has 30 actions, and that it is meant to be iterative.

Councillors raised area municipality engagement. Staff said they had emailed CAOs and met municipal staff leads but acknowledged the engagement fell short of what was wanted. Others said the plan lacks detail on youth and children's services, the justice system, women-focused supports and private sector involvement. One councillor asked that the advocacy strategy be accelerated.

Supporters of moving ahead said the situation is urgent and the plan can be refined later. For the child care item, councillors asked who could use the spaces and noted the City of Kitchener owns the Kitchener land, so an indemnification with the City will be needed. Staff agreed to include it.
